## Engineering discipline

This repository vendors a Python engineering discipline at `'), FormattedValue(Name('agent_dir', Load()), -1), Constant('/discipline/`.
**Read `'), FormattedValue(Name('agent_dir', Load()), -1), Constant("/discipline/KERNEL.md` before writing Python here.** It is about
1,800 tokens and carries the thesis, the always-apply invariants and a router to the
rest; everything else is loaded on demand.

The thesis: *a failure must be machine-diagnosable and machine-repairable* — an agent
meeting a defect should be able to name what broke, where, in which layer, against which
contract, from the program's own output. Deep error traceability and least coupling exist
to serve that. Anything mechanically verifiable shall be mechanically verified.

Do not read the modules speculatively. Ask instead:

```bash
python "), FormattedValue(Name('agent_dir', Load()), -1), Constant('/tools/nav.py context --file <path> --error "<message>"
python '), FormattedValue(Name('agent_dir', Load()), -1), Constant('/tools/nav.py applies <path>          # which rules govern this file
python '), FormattedValue(Name('agent_dir', Load()), -1), Constant('/tools/learn.py retrieve --file <path> --error "<message>"
```

Before reporting done, record what this session learned about this repository — or that
it learned nothing:

```bash
python '), FormattedValue(Name('agent_dir', Load()), -1), Constant('/tools/learn.py record --kind diagnostic \
    --claim "..." --action "..." --trigger "error:..." --link RULE-ID
```

Every element of the code carries a documentation comment in Doxygen form; see
`'), FormattedValue(Name('agent_dir', Load()), -1), Constant('/discipline/law/DOC.md`. The gate is `ruff check`, `mypy`, `pytest`,
`lint-imports` and the checks under `'), FormattedValue(Name('agent_dir', Load()), -1), Constant('/enforce/`.

Rule ids such as `ARCH-002` and `DIAG-005` are stable — cite them in review comments and
commit messages.
